subject: Issues using MS m-array model from jags in nimble

messages.author: 6cbadef44c761177
messages.subject: Issues using MS m-array model from jags in nimble
parts:
Hi all,

I am new to Nimble - I took a workshop back at TWS in Reno but that has been my only introduction to the program. I am hoping to use Nimble to fit an integrated population model I have been working on for some time in Jags. By all accounts, the model should converge (I have checked with simulated data, sub-models, used informative priors/inits, etc.) but after 500k iterations, two parameters (which happen to have the most data) just will not converge. So, I am hoping to get this model up and running in Nimble to customize some samplers and see if it will work there.

I am using a multi-state m-array to fit my survival sub-model and am having an issue transitioning from the jags code to fitting the model in Nimble. I have attached the code I am working with (ipm_nimble.R). I am getting the following error:

Error in replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) : 
  Error, hit end
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) :
  Code ones was given as known but evaluates to a non-scalar.  This is probably not what you want.
2: In replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) :
  Code ones was given as known but evaluates to a non-scalar.  This is probably not what you want.
3: In replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) :
  Code zero was given as known but evaluates to a non-scalar.  This is probably not what you want.

I expect these errors refer specifically to Defining the cell probabilities of the m-array (specifically lines 239, 244, 259). Code was adapted from Kery and Schaub. I apologize if this is an elementary level question. Any help you could provide would be immensely helpful!

Kylee Dunham

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Issues using MS m-array model from jags in nimble
parts:
Hi Kylee,

I suggest two resources for you, both linked from our documentation page: https://r-nimble.org/documentation-2

The first is the blog post on converting from JAGS to NIMBLE.  For your declarations involving "zero" and "ones" on the right-hand side, you will need explicit indexing, such as "zero[1:ns, 1:ns]".  There may be other issues, but those jump out as relevant from the error messages and looking at your code.

The second is the nimbleEcology package, which includes Hidden Markov Model distributions relevant for multi-state mark-recapture: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/nimbleEcology/index.html

I think most people end up switching away from writing code out to a file and instead using nimbleCode within R.

HTH
-Perry

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Issues using MS m-array model from jags in nimble
parts:
Can you please try forming your index blocks as follows and let us know if it resolves the problem:

Instead of
 U[(t-1)*ns+(1:ns), (j-1)*ns+(1:ns)]
please try
 U[ ((t-1)*ns+1):((t-1)*ns + ns), ((j-1)*ns+1):((j-1)*ns + ns)]
(which I guess is the same as:
 U[ ((t-1)*ns+1):(t*ns), ((j-1)*ns+1):(j*ns)]
)
and similar in other places.

-Perry
